{{Short description|Objects between rings and their fields of fractions}}
In [[mathematics]], '''almost modules''' and '''almost rings''' are certain objects interpolating between [[commutative ring| rings]] and their [[field of fractions|fields of fractions]]. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Faltings|first=Gerd|authorlink=Gerd Faltings|year=1988}} in his study of [[p-adic Hodge theory|''p''-adic Hodge theory]].

==Almost modules==
Let ''V'' be a [[local ring|local]] [[integral domain]] with the [[maximal ideal]] ''m'', and ''K'' a [[fraction field]] of ''V''. The [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of ''K''-[[Module (mathematics)|modules]], ''K''-'''Mod''', may be obtained as a [[Quotient of an abelian category|quotient]] of ''V''-'''Mod''' by the [[Serre subcategory]] of [[torsion module]]s, i.e. those ''N'' such that any element ''n'' in ''N'' is annihilated by some nonzero element in the maximal ideal. If the category of torsion modules is replaced by a smaller [[subcategory]], we obtain an intermediate step between ''V''-modules and ''K''-modules. Faltings proposed to use the subcategory of '''almost zero''' modules, i.e. ''N'' ∈ ''V''-'''Mod''' such that any element ''n'' in ''N'' is annihilated by ''all'' elements of the maximal ideal.

For this idea to work, ''m'' and ''V'' must satisfy certain technical conditions. Let ''V'' be a [[Ring (mathematics)|ring]] (not necessarily local) and ''m'' ⊆ ''V'' an idempotent [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]], i.e. an ideal such that ''m''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m''. Assume also that ''m''&nbsp;&otimes;&nbsp;''m'' is a [[Flat module|flat]] ''V''-module. A module ''N'' over ''V'' is '''almost zero''' with respect to such ''m'' if for all ''ε'' ∈ ''m'' and ''n'' ∈ ''N'' we have ''εn'' = 0. Almost zero modules form a Serre subcategory of the category of ''V''-modules. The category of ''almost V-modules'', ''V''<sup>{{space|hair}}''a''</sup>-'''Mod''', is a [[Quotient of an abelian category|localization]] of ''V''-'''Mod''' along this subcategory.

The quotient [[functor]] ''V''-'''Mod''' → ''V''<sup>{{space|hair}}''a''</sup>-'''Mod''' is denoted by <math>N \mapsto N^a</math>. The assumptions on ''m'' guarantee that <math>(-)^a</math> is an [[exact functor]] which has both the right [[adjoint functor]] <math> M \mapsto M_*</math> and the left adjoint functor <math>M \mapsto M_!</math>. Moreover, <math>(-)_*</math> is [[Full and faithful functors|full and faithful]]. The category of almost modules is [[Complete category|complete]] and [[Complete category|cocomplete]].

== Almost rings ==

The [[tensor product of modules| tensor product]] of ''V''-modules descends to a [[monoidal category | monoidal structure]] on ''V''<sup>{{space|hair}}''a''</sup>-'''Mod'''. An almost module ''R'' ∈ ''V''<sup>{{space|hair}}''a''</sup>-'''Mod''' with a map ''R'' ⊗ ''R'' → ''R'' satisfying natural conditions, similar to a definition of a ring, is called an '''almost ''V''-algebra''' or an '''almost ring''' if the context is unambiguous. Many standard properties of algebras and morphisms between them carry to the "almost" world.

===Example===

In the original paper by Faltings, ''V'' was the [[integral element|integral closure]] of a [[discrete valuation ring]] in the [[algebraic closure]] of its [[Field of fractions|quotient field]], and ''m'' its maximal ideal. For example, let ''V'' be <math>\mathbb{Z}_p[p^{1/p^{\infty}}]</math>, i.e. a ''p''-adic [[Completion (algebra) | completion]] of <math> \operatorname{colim}\limits_n \mathbb{Z}_p[p^{1/p^n}]</math>. Take ''m'' to be the maximal ideal of this ring. Then the quotient ''V/m'' is an almost zero module, while ''V/p'' is a torsion, but not almost zero module since the class of ''p''<sup>1/''p''<sup>2</sup></sup> in the quotient is not annihilated by ''p''<sup>1/''p''<sup>2</sup></sup> considered as an element of ''m''.
